title: ID S1227: Adds to existing law to establish provisions regarding generative artificial intelligence in public education.

obligations: The State Department of Education shall develop a statewide generative artificial intelligence in education framework, subject to State Board of Education approval, for use in K 12 Idaho public schools; the framework shall prioritize human centered oversight, transparency, safety, and data security; provide guidance on instructional integration, academic integrity, digital citizenship, and responsible student use; address accessibility, accommodations, and access to generative AI tools; and serve as the foundation for local school district and public charter school policies, professional development, procurement practices, and statewide standards (Sec. 33-7003(1)).

The framework shall be reviewed and updated as needed through a process led by the State Department of Education, which shall convene education practitioners, industry partners, and workforce representatives to ensure the framework reflects emerging technologies, risks, and best practices (Sec. 33-7003(2)).

Each local school district and public charter school shall adopt a policy governing the use of generative artificial intelligence by students and employees in school buildings, on school grounds, during school activities, and on school issued devices; the policy shall align with the statewide framework, define appropriate and prohibited uses of generative AI for instructional, administrative, and communication purposes, include safeguards for student privacy, data security, accessibility, and academic integrity, and comply with all applicable state and federal laws, including Idaho student data privacy requirements, the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act, the Children's Internet Protection Act, and the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (Sec. 33-7004).

The State Department of Education, in consultation with educators, industry partners, and technology experts, shall develop and recommend to the State Board of Education generative AI literacy standards for K 12 students, assessment guidelines to evaluate student understanding of generative AI concepts, ethics, and responsible use, and a professional development plan to build educator capacity in safe and effective integration of generative AI technologies (Sec. 33-7005).

The State Department of Education shall develop for parents and legal guardians a generative AI guidance document to support transparency and public understanding of generative AI in public education (Sec. 33-7006).

All generative AI related software, applications, and tools procured by local school districts and public charter schools shall comply with state and federal data privacy laws, including the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act, the Children's Internet Protection Act, and the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act; vendors shall disclose whether products utilize machine learning, predictive analytics, or generative AI and shall provide assurances regarding data protection, algorithmic transparency, and responsible use (Sec. 33-7007(1)).
prohibitions: No specific prohibited uses are stated in the statute; each local school district and public charter school policy must define appropriate and prohibited uses of generative AI for instructional, administrative, and communication purposes (Sec. 33-7004(2)).

What it does

This chapter requires the Idaho State Department of Education to develop a statewide generative artificial intelligence in education framework, subject to State Board of Education approval, for K 12 public schools. It requires local school districts and public charter schools to adopt policies governing generative AI use by students and employees, and it directs the State Department of Education to develop literacy standards, assessment guidelines, professional development, and a parental guidance document. It also imposes procurement and vendor disclosure requirements for generative AI tools and grants the State Board of Education rulemaking authority.

Who it applies to

  • State Department of Education
  • State Board of Education
  • local school districts
  • public charter schools
  • vendors of generative AI related software, applications, and tools

Effective date

July 1, 2026

Key definitions

  • Generative artificial intelligence or generative AI: artificial intelligence models that use machine learning and are trained on large volumes of data that can generate new content; when prompted, generative AI can create various outputs, including text, images, videos, computer code, and music; generative AI does not include artificial intelligence models that have the primary goal of classifying data, such as those used in automated vehicles (Sec. 33-7002(1)).
  • Generative artificial intelligence in education: the responsible use of generative artificial intelligence technologies to support instruction, enhance student engagement, personalize learning, improve administrative efficiency, or assist educator decision making while ensuring that human judgment remains the final authority (Sec. 33-7002(2)).

Obligations

  • The State Department of Education shall develop a statewide generative artificial intelligence in education framework, subject to State Board of Education approval, for use in K 12 Idaho public schools; the framework shall prioritize human centered oversight, transparency, safety, and data security; provide guidance on instructional integration, academic integrity, digital citizenship, and responsible student use; address accessibility, accommodations, and access to generative AI tools; and serve as the foundation for local school district and public charter school policies, professional development, procurement practices, and statewide standards (Sec. 33-7003(1)).
  • The framework shall be reviewed and updated as needed through a process led by the State Department of Education, which shall convene education practitioners, industry partners, and workforce representatives to ensure the framework reflects emerging technologies, risks, and best practices (Sec. 33-7003(2)).
  • Each local school district and public charter school shall adopt a policy governing the use of generative artificial intelligence by students and employees in school buildings, on school grounds, during school activities, and on school issued devices; the policy shall align with the statewide framework, define appropriate and prohibited uses of generative AI for instructional, administrative, and communication purposes, include safeguards for student privacy, data security, accessibility, and academic integrity, and comply with all applicable state and federal laws, including Idaho student data privacy requirements, the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act, the Children's Internet Protection Act, and the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (Sec. 33-7004).
  • The State Department of Education, in consultation with educators, industry partners, and technology experts, shall develop and recommend to the State Board of Education generative AI literacy standards for K 12 students, assessment guidelines to evaluate student understanding of generative AI concepts, ethics, and responsible use, and a professional development plan to build educator capacity in safe and effective integration of generative AI technologies (Sec. 33-7005).
  • The State Department of Education shall develop for parents and legal guardians a generative AI guidance document to support transparency and public understanding of generative AI in public education (Sec. 33-7006).
  • All generative AI related software, applications, and tools procured by local school districts and public charter schools shall comply with state and federal data privacy laws, including the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act, the Children's Internet Protection Act, and the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act; vendors shall disclose whether products utilize machine learning, predictive analytics, or generative AI and shall provide assurances regarding data protection, algorithmic transparency, and responsible use (Sec. 33-7007(1)).

Prohibitions

  • No specific prohibited uses are stated in the statute; each local school district and public charter school policy must define appropriate and prohibited uses of generative AI for instructional, administrative, and communication purposes (Sec. 33-7004(2)).

Penalties and enforcement

The statute does not state who enforces it or what penalties apply. It grants the State Board of Education rulemaking authority, subject to legislative approval, to implement the provisions of this chapter (Sec. 33-7008). No private right of action is stated in the text.

How it affects AI deployment

  • Any generative AI tool used in Idaho K 12 public schools must be governed by a local school district or public charter school policy that aligns with the statewide framework and covers use by students and employees in school buildings, on school grounds, during school activities, and on school issued devices (Sec. 33-7004).
  • Vendors of generative AI related software, applications, and tools must disclose whether their products utilize machine learning, predictive analytics, or generative AI and must provide assurances regarding data protection, algorithmic transparency, and responsible use before procurement by a local school district or public charter school (Sec. 33-7007(1)).
  • All generative AI related software, applications, and tools procured by local school districts and public charter schools must comply with state and federal data privacy laws, including FERPA, CIPA, and COPPA (Sec. 33-7007(1)).
  • Human judgment must remain the final authority in any use of generative artificial intelligence in education, meaning AI cannot replace educator decision making (Sec. 33-7002(2)).
  • The statewide framework prioritizes human centered oversight, transparency, safety, and data security, and addresses accessibility, accommodations, and access to generative AI tools, so deployments must meet these priorities (Sec. 33-7003(1)).
  • The State Department of Education may establish a list of approved generative AI tools or model procurement guidelines, which could restrict which tools local school districts and public charter schools may procure (Sec. 33-7007(2)).
  • Generative AI literacy standards, assessment guidelines, and professional development will be developed and recommended, so schools deploying AI will need to align instruction and educator training with those standards once approved (Sec. 33-7005).

Notable exemptions

  • Generative AI does not include artificial intelligence models that have the primary goal of classifying data, such as those used in automated vehicles (Sec. 33-7002(1)).

Compliance steps

  • Review the statewide generative artificial intelligence in education framework once it is approved by the State Board of Education (Sec. 33-7003(1)).
  • Adopt a policy governing generative AI use by students and employees in school buildings, on school grounds, during school activities, and on school issued devices, aligning with the statewide framework, defining appropriate and prohibited uses, including safeguards for student privacy, data security, accessibility, and academic integrity, and complying with applicable state and federal laws (Sec. 33-7004).
  • Ensure any generative AI related software, applications, and tools procured comply with state and federal data privacy laws, including FERPA, CIPA, and COPPA, and obtain vendor disclosures and assurances regarding data protection, algorithmic transparency, and responsible use (Sec. 33-7007(1)).
  • Consult any list of approved generative AI tools or model procurement guidelines established by the State Department of Education when procuring generative AI tools (Sec. 33-7007(2)).
  • Implement generative AI literacy standards, assessment guidelines, and professional development once recommended by the State Department of Education and approved by the State Board of Education (Sec. 33-7005).
  • Follow any rules promulgated by the State Board of Education under its rulemaking authority (Sec. 33-7008).
